questions.prompt: A claude-code-action workflow has no prompt input. What does Claude do?

options.text: It waits for @claude in a comment, then replies there
options.explanation: Right. That is interactive mode. The trigger phrase is @claude by default.

options.text: It runs on every push and writes to the run log
options.explanation: That is closer to automation mode, which needs a prompt input.

options.text: It refuses to start and the workflow fails
options.explanation: No prompt input is a normal setup: Claude waits for a mention.

questions.prompt: Where do you write repo rules for Codex code review on GitHub?

options.text: In a REVIEW.md file at the repo root
options.explanation: REVIEW.md is a file Claude Code Review reads. Codex reads AGENTS.md.

options.text: In a Code Review Rules section of AGENTS.md
options.explanation: Right. Codex follows the ## Code Review Rules section in the AGENTS.md closest to the changed code.

options.text: In the commit message of each pull request
options.explanation: OpenAI's page puts review rules in AGENTS.md files.

questions.prompt: Can the Claude Code Review check run block a merge by itself?

options.text: Yes, whenever it finds an Important issue
options.explanation: Findings are tagged by severity but don't block the PR.

options.text: Yes, once branch protection lists the check
options.explanation: The check run always ends neutral, so branch protection never sees a failure.

options.text: No, it always completes with a neutral result
options.explanation: Right. To gate merges, read its severity counts in your own CI.
